We talk about sugar, cholesterol, protein, workout, badminton, core strength, ageing, discipline, and yet we eat like a college student who has just discovered unlimited Tamil Nadu meals.

And that’s why in our house, the weighing machine has a very important role. 

It is hidden under the bed in our master bedroom – the one in which Rekha sleeps with her AC at 18 degrees. 

I don’t know if we put the weighing machine there, or it hides there by itself after ruining our day.

Rekha and I both watch our weight, but there is a difference. 

Whenever I stand on the circle of shame (the shape of our weighing machine), I tell Rekha my weight. 

But she never tells me hers.

She says, “I have lost 400 grams in last one week,” but never gives away the absolute number. 

This hurts more because when we got married in 2004, she was 49 Kgs. 

And by a stretch, she was my 50 kg Taj Mahal…if you know Tamil and have heard the song ‘Fifty kg Taj-u Mahal enakae enaka’ from the 1998 movie Jeans starring Aishwarya Rai, you will know what I mean. 

For those who don’t know Tamil the song’s lyrics means, ‘The 50 Kg Taj Mahal for me…”

Her current weight has been one of the great unsolved mysteries of our marriage.

I have known Rekha for more than twenty-five years. 

I know her moods, when she is angry, the moment she is going to say ‘fine!’ and when she is going to say ‘nothing.’ 

I know which sarees she likes, which handbags she likes, which shops she trusts, which of her friends she doesn’t trust, and which restaurants she thinks are overrated.

But I do not know her weight. 

Finding out Rekha’s actual weight is like finding out how much money the British took out of India. 

I have an estimated number, but if you asked me how I arrived at that number, I can’t explain.

----X----X----

I don’t check my weight daily because I am not disciplined. I do so only on special occasions.

For example, if I have played badminton for a long time and sweated a lot, I will come back home with the confidence of a man who has burnt at least 7,000 calories, and stand on the weighing machine.

But the weighing machine is very disciplined. 

It disappoints me every time.

I go there thinking, “Today surely I must have lost at least 500 grams.”

But no, the machine will show me the same weight I had a few days back.

Sometimes, after a heavy workout, I stand on it… only to see the same number.

Then I will remove my watch, hoping against hope and yet it again it will be the same number.

They say air is weightless, but why take a chance. 

So I breathe out and then stand on the scale….but see the same number.

Then, like all desperate men, I suck in my stomach.

And since I haven’t come out of the master bedroom for five minutes, like all dutiful wife Rekha will walk in to check if everything is alright. 

She will see me sucking my stomach while standing on the scale and say, “I don’t think that helps.”

Of course it helps, because when I suck in my stomach I don’t have to crane my neck to see the numbers. 

But I won’t explain it all to her.

I will quickly get off the scale and slide it under the bed, because I don’t want my wife to see the number on the scale.
 
I like telling my weight to her myself…because that helps me make morally justifiable adjustments. 

Basically small adjustments that don’t harm her, but show me in better light in her eyes. 

For example, if I have lost only 100 grams, I may end up saying “Rekha…lost 300 grams.”

She would smile, and say, “Rajan….that’s good. No?”

I will nod, and my life would start feeling fine all over again. 

In 2016, when I gave up corporate life, and started my own business, I was 78 kilos.

Today, without any dieting, but with three days of heavy workout and three days of heavy badminton almost every week, I am usually between 70 and 71 kilos.

Effectively, I have lost 7 to 8 kilos over the years.

The problem is that I have never been able to go below 70. 

That number is like my Wagah border…I can go near it….look across it…but I can’t cross it. 

No matter what I do, the weighing machine stops me at 70. 

It is as if Rekha has had a private conversation with the weighing scale: “Whatever happens, don’t let him become too happy.”

----X----X----

The funny thing is, whenever I weigh myself, I tell Rekha. 

But if I ask her, “What is your weight?” She won’t reply. 

She will pretend as if she hasn’t heard it. 

Worse still, she will bring up some task that’s still pending and ask for its status. 

I have even tried indirect approaches. 

“Rekha, as we grow older BMI is important. Shall we calculate ours?”

She didn’t fall for it.

Then one day, as I lay next to her, and she seemed vulnerable, I asked her, “After all these years, we don’t have any secrets between us…right?”

She didn’t even turn towards me…she continued to look at the ceiling fan and said, “Many.”

That one word was enough to freeze me in my place because marriage is not about knowing everything…it is about knowing when to stop asking. 

If there are a few things Rekha is keeping a secret from me, then I sure as hell don’t want to know. 

She is doing that because I may get hurt if I know. 

That works for me too, which is why I don’t tell her about my girlfriends. 

But however hard she may try to hide it, I know when she has had a bad day on the weighing scale. 

The weighing machine may have given her the number, but it is me who faces the consequences.

Some days she will come out of the master bedroom and suddenly I will be responsible for everything wrong in the house.

“Why is this towel here?”

“Why are the lights on?”

“Why is this charger lying here?”

“Why are you sitting like you have lost something?”

I know the pattern so when something like this happens, I keep a low profile. 

I avoid talking, burping, and farting. 

On an average I breath about 14 to 16 times per minute, and on days when the weighing machine has shown her a number she is not happy with, I bring it down to 12 to 13 times so as to not disturb her.

But a husband can’t always be careful enough. 

In marriage, many disasters begin with the husband trying to help.

So one day when Rekha was not happy with the weighing machine, I told her that I had an idea. 

She looked at me with suspicion. 

Because she has lived with me long enough to know that my ideas come in two categories: useless and dangerous.

I said, “Why don’t you lie down on the floor, lift both your legs up at 90 degrees to your body, and I will place the weighing scale on your feet?”

She stared at me. I continued, because men never know when to stop.

“That way the scale will show a lower number.”

Technically, I am not even sure whether this is true.

But Rekha did not reply. 

Neither did she laugh….which meant, it wasn’t funny as well. 

That day I realised that women do not appreciate scientific innovation when they are upset with their weight.

After a few hours she asked, “Do you think I am overweight?”

Before I tell you what I responded with, you need to know that we Rajans are lovable creatures. 

For us, one only needs to be a woman to fall in love. 

Tall or short, fat or thin, fair or dark, rich or poor…doesn’t matter. 

All that we need is for you to be a woman.

Now, I can’t go back to Rekha with that reply, can I? So I said, “Of course not. And even if you were, that’s just more of you to love.”

There was silence from the other end. 

Now when your wife is silent, it augurs well for the husband to also remain silent. 

Later that night Rekha asked, “Do you want to start dieting?”

I don’t remember what happened over the next half hour…I have faint memory of not wanting to diet…but I also remember saying, “Ok, let’s do it together!”

And the next day we skipped our regular tea and had green tea.

And we reduced the quantity of rice intake, and we stuck to a lot of greens. 

The whole day, looked at each other with respect.

The next day we went for the core workout, which we have been paying for the last one year, but skipping more times that attending. 

During the first week of green tea, and core workouts, we would check weight often – as soon as we got up, after a bath when still in a towel, before going to bed, etc – but we didn’t notice anything. 

I usually don’t care but Rekha takes dieting seriously and loves to see results. 

After a week she sprung a surprise, “What is this Rajan…is it even worth it?”

I would have given up right then, but then I knew Rekha wanted to try this out, for the 100th time, once again. So didn’t give up. 

“Yes Rekha…let’s keep at it for two weeks and then take a call,” I said and gave her hope. 

So we continued to consume only green tea, and maintain the rest of the drama.

One day I came back home slightly early, and saw Rekha watching ‘Pritam and Pedro’ on Netflix. 

Right next to her was a Tupperware with her favourite snack – Madras Mixture. 

The biggest enemy of weight loss in our house is not rice but Tupperware containers, which in our house are available in three sizes.

In these containers, we store dry fruits, different kinds of biscuits, snacks, mixtures, murukku, and many other items that are not technically meals but can quietly become one.

There are at least ten to twelve such containers in the house at any given time.

Which means that in our house, food is always available. This is where WTF becomes our family motto. 

When Rekha sits in front of the TV, she will sometimes take two-three such containers. 

This is normal, and all of us do that. 

But my problem is, when one of them gets over, and my daughter and I look for it, Rekha will refuse that she had anything to do with its disappearance. 

“No, no. It was almost over when I took it from the kitchen shelf,” is her standard line and she doesn’t budge 

Rhea and I don’t believe her. We have seen patterns repeating…just that we don’t have it documented. 

Now we are wondering whether we should install CCTV in the hall, not for security, but to find out who is finishing the snacks.

I cannot make too much fun of Rekha and her love for snacks because I have my own weakness - peanuts. 

I am a huge fan of peanuts and have it at all occasions. 

I love them because they come in many forms - salted peanuts, masala peanuts, fried peanuts, boiled peanuts…kind of like the rats in Pied Piper of Hamelin.

I can have peanuts with Old Monk, without Old Monk…I can have them when I am happy, when I am sad or when I am writing.

If there is one food item that has stood by me through good times and bad times, it is peanuts. 

Unfortunately, my body has not handled this relationship well because now I have high cholesterol.

When I was young, my mother used to say cholesterol is a rich man’s disease. 

This made sense then because only the rich ate butter, cheese, meat, sweets, cashews, and things we saw only on Doordarshan.

So if cholesterol is a rich man’s disease and I now have it, I can only conclude one thing – I am going to be rich soon.

And when that happens I plan to hire a weighing machine operator. 

His job will be like that of a lift operator…he will be next to the weighing machine…and once you stand on it…he will speak out the number. 

But the best part is, he will also motivate us when we feel let down. 

“Ma’am, it could be because of the weight of your jeans!”

“Sir, remember last night you had a drinks party…must be all that food.”

Just that, we may have to move the weighing machine to the living room…because I can’t have another man standing inside our master bedroom.

I believe a weighing machine doesn’t just weigh us…it also measures our hope….our confidence. 

Every time we stand on it, we are not just checking kilos but also seeing if yesterday’s sacrifice mattered.

And that’s why we need a “confidence booster” right next to the weighing machine. 

And my idea may work, because hope and confidence are just like weight – they keep returning.

text:
This wouldn't be a problem if jury cases were handled similarly to how they were previously in America.

In the 19th century, jury cases lasted hours - maybe a day or two at most.

In the first half of the 20th century, most cases still wrapped up within a day or two.

It was only in the second half of the 20th century -especially in the 1950s and 1960s - that jury trials routinely lasted days, and then eventually weeks.

I was just involved in a civil trial over a business dispute that lasted two months.  TWO MONTHS.  We went in thinking maybe it would last three weeks - and even that was too long for us.  Anyone who has paid for lawyer fees knows that the difference between three and eight weeks is not trivial.

But think of it from the jury's perspective.  It was entirely made up of women, some without jobs and some with trivial jobs - none with business experience.  Why?  What serious working person wants to take three to eight weeks off from work to listen to some business dispute?  They started off respectful of the process and by the end they were completely bored with the proceedings.  And rightly so.

Jury trials have become such a problem that the American legal system started getting rid of them a few decades ago.  Very few cases now go to trial because both sides rightly fear the cost and the potential result.

The Lindsay Clancy trial lasted seven weeks - six weeks of trial proceedings and one week of deliberations.  Think of that.  SEVEN WEEKS OF TIME when who murdered the three children was never in doubt for one second.  Instead, the jury spent the entire time negotiating the gutters of how modern psychiatry intersects with Massachusetts state law to get inside Lindsay Clancy's mind.  They might as well have spent the time researching how Puritans rooted out witches.

text:
Leo Frank tried to frame his Negro nightwatchman Newt Lee with three pieces of forged evidence: Death Notes dictated by Frank and "ghost written" by Jim Conley to frame Newt Lee, a Forged Time Card to incriminate Newt Lee, a Planted Blood soaked shirt at Newt Lees home to seal the deal. 

The Newt Lee Time Slip: Who Saw It Before and After It Changed

How Leo Frank Used Newt Lee’s Time Card to Turn Suspicion Toward His Night Watchman

The case that Leo Frank altered or manipulated Newt Lee’s time card does not depend on one witness, one newspaper story, or something somebody came up with years later. It comes from several people who were standing around the time clock on Sunday morning, April 27, 1913, when Frank took Lee’s original Saturday-night slip out of the machine, looked at it, and said it was correct.

Then something changed.

On Sunday, Frank said the card was right. Newt Lee said Frank told him he had missed no punches. W. W. “Boots” Rogers personally looked down the card and said there was “a punch for every number.” N. V. Darley looked over Frank’s shoulder and agreed it was all right.

By Monday, Frank was saying the card was wrong.

By Tuesday morning, police were searching Newt Lee’s home because the newly discovered missing time supposedly gave Lee enough time to leave the factory, go home, and come back. At about 9 o’clock Tuesday morning, April 29, Detective John R. Black found a bloody shirt at the bottom of a clothes barrel inside Lee’s home.

Sunday.

Monday.

Tuesday.

Like clockwork.

The important part is who actually saw the time slip before and after this change.

Who Was Standing at the Time Clock Sunday Morning?

Newt Lee gave the clearest list.

In his sworn trial testimony, Lee said:

“Boots Rogers, Chief Langford, Darley, Mr. Frank and I were there when they opened the clock.”

Lee then said:

“Mr. Frank opened the clock and said the punches were all right, that I hadn’t missed any punches.”

Lee was very specific about his own rounds. He said:

“I punched every half hour from six o’clock until three o’clock, which was the last punch I made” (Brief of Evidence, 1).

So according to Lee, the people positively standing there when the clock was opened were Leo Frank, Newt Lee, W. W. “Boots” Rogers, N. V. Darley, and Chief of Detectives Newport A. Lanford.

Detective John R. Black also testified that he saw Frank take the slip out of the clock and go back toward his office with it. Black therefore places himself at the scene as well, although Lee did not include Black in his own five-man list (Brief of Evidence, 1).

I would not add Detective Starnes to the list of people who personally heard Frank pronounce the slip correct. Starnes later testified that he was not present when Frank referred to Newt Lee’s punch-slip record. There were plenty of witnesses without stretching the list (AJ, 3).

Boots Rogers Did More Than Hear Frank Say It Was Correct

W. W. “Boots” Rogers is important because he did not simply hear Frank say the card was all right. He looked at it himself.

Rogers testified at Frank’s trial on Wednesday morning, July 30, 1913, after court reconvened at 9 o’clock. The Atlanta Journal, Wednesday, July 30, 1913, page 4, column 1, reported his testimony.

According to Rogers, after the group returned from inspecting the basement and prepared to go to police headquarters, Frank said to Darley:

“I had better put in a new slip, hadn’t I, Darley?”

Darley agreed.

Frank took out his keys, unlocked the right-hand time clock, removed Lee’s slip, looked at it, and said it had been punched correctly.

Rogers then examined it for himself.

His sworn testimony in the Brief of Evidence was:

“I looked at the slip that Mr. Frank took out (Defendant’s Exhibit I), the first punch was 6:01, the second one was 6:32 or 6:33. He took the slip back in his office. I glanced all the way down and there was a punch for every number” (Brief of Evidence, 1).

That is one of the strongest pieces of evidence in this whole time-card issue.

Rogers did not say, “Frank told me it was correct, so I assumed it was.”

He looked at the card.

He remembered the first two punches.

He looked down the entire thing.

And he saw “a punch for every number.”

Then Frank took the slip back into his office.

The Atlanta Journal, Wednesday, July 30, 1913, page 4, column 1, gave essentially the same account. Frank removed the slip, pronounced it all right, laid it down, went into his office for another slip, and several of the men looked at the original while he was gone (AJ, 3).

N. V. Darley Was Looking Over Frank’s Shoulder

N. V. Darley was not standing across the room trying to remember something he had barely seen. He said he was looking over Frank’s shoulder.

Darley testified at the trial on Friday, August 1, 1913:

“I was present on Sunday morning when the time slip was taken out. I was looking over Mr. Frank’s shoulder.”

He continued:

“Mr. Frank looked down the number side and said it was all right and I verified it” (Brief of Evidence, 1).

Darley later acknowledged something important. He had not noticed the long intervals between 9:32 and 10:29, 11:04 and 12:00, and 2:03 and 3:01.

His explanation was that he and Frank had looked down the numbered side. Every numbered line had an entry, so at first glance the card looked complete.

That became Frank’s explanation too.

But there is no dispute over the basic Sunday-morning event.

Frank said the card was right.

Darley agreed.

Rogers agreed.

Lee heard it.

And police were standing there.

Newt Lee Gives the Sunday-to-Monday Change Under Oath

The cleanest evidence of the actual Sunday-to-Monday reversal comes from Newt Lee at the coroner’s inquest.

On Wednesday morning, April 30, 1913, Lee was questioned under oath. The Atlanta Georgian, Wednesday, April 30, 1913, printed the questions and answers.

Lee was asked:

“Did you punch your clock every half-hour Saturday night?”

He answered:

“Yes, sir; every half-hour from 6 o’clock until I found the body.”

Then:

Q. “What did Mr. Frank say to you Sunday morning?”

A. “He said the clock had been punched all right.”

Then they asked again:

Q. “Did he say the clock had been punched regularly?”

A. “Yes, sir.”

A little later the questioning came back to it:

Q. “Did Mr. Frank say the clock was punched all right?”

Lee answered:

“Yes, sir; on Sunday morning he said I had never lost a punch.”

Then came the question that changes the whole thing:

Q. “Did Mr. Frank ever tell you that the clock was not punched regularly last Saturday night?”

Lee answered:

“Yes, sir; he told me on Monday morning that the clock was not punched right” (AG, 2).

There is the Sunday-to-Monday change in plain English.

Sunday: Frank tells Lee he never lost a punch.

Monday: Frank tells Lee the card was not punched right.

No modern interpretation is required.

Lee testified to it three days after the murder.

Detective John Black Gives Independent Police Corroboration

Detective John R. Black gave the other major before-and-after account.

Black testified at Frank’s trial on Wednesday, July 30, 1913, with the important time-slip questioning continuing during the afternoon session.

His testimony was very specific:

“At the pencil factory Mr. Frank took the slip out, looked over it and said it had been punched correctly.”

Then Black immediately added:

“On Monday and Tuesday following Mr. Frank stated that the clock had been mispunched three times” (Brief of Evidence, 1).

That is about as direct as it gets.

Black gives us both sides himself.

Sunday: correctly punched.

Monday and Tuesday: mispunched three times.

Black also testified that Frank said he did not believe Newt Lee had told everything he knew about the murder. According to Black, Frank said the incorrectly punched card:

“would have given Lee an hour to have gone out to his house and back” (Brief of Evidence, 1).

This is when the time-card discrepancy stopped being an innocent curiosity and became useful against Newt Lee.

The missing time now supplied an opportunity.

If Lee had an unaccounted-for hour, police could argue that he left the factory, went home, changed clothes, disposed of something, and returned before his next recorded punch.

That is exactly where the bloody shirt enters the story.

What Happened to the Slip Between Sunday and Monday?

This is where the chain of custody gets muddy.

Rogers said Frank took the original slip “back in his office” after removing it from the clock (Brief of Evidence, 1).

Black testified:

“I saw Mr. Frank take it out of the clock and went back with it toward his office.”

Black also said the slip was turned over to Chief Lanford on Monday, but then immediately qualified himself:

“I don’t know of my own personal knowledge that it was turned over to Chief Lanford Monday” (Brief of Evidence, 1).

Frank later gave a different account in his unsworn statement on Monday, August 18, 1913. Frank said he brought the slip to the office and Chief Lanford put it in his pocket Sunday morning. Frank also said he and Darley had only casually checked the numbered lines and had not compared the actual times between punches (Brief of Evidence, 1).

So even the custody story is disputed.

Rogers says Frank took it into his office.

Black says he saw Frank take it toward his office and could not personally swear when Lanford received it.

Frank says Lanford took possession Sunday morning.

That does not by itself prove alteration, but it leaves a hole right where you do not want one when dealing with a piece of physical evidence that later changed the direction of the investigation.

Tuesday Morning: Police Search Newt Lee’s Home

Detective Black testified that at approximately 9 o’clock Tuesday morning, April 29, 1913, he searched Newt Lee’s home at the rear of 40 Henry Street.

He said:

“I found a bloody shirt in the bottom of a clothes barrel there” (Brief of Evidence, 1).

Black later added:

“The blood looks like it is on both sides of the shirt” (Brief of Evidence, 1).

Now put the three days together.

Sunday, April 27: Frank says Lee’s time card is correctly punched. Rogers sees a punch for every number. Darley looks over Frank’s shoulder and agrees.

Monday, April 28: Frank is now saying the card has been mispunched. Lee testifies Frank told him Monday morning the clock was not punched right. Black says Frank began pointing to missing time that could have allowed Lee to go home.

Tuesday, April 29, about 9 o’clock: Black searches Lee’s home and finds a bloody shirt in a clothes barrel.

Sunday.

Monday.

Tuesday.

JUST Like clockwork.

Did Frank’s Statement About the Missing Time Cause the Search?

Black’s testimony here has to be handled carefully because Rosser got him crossed up on the exact order of events.

On redirect examination Black said the search of Lee’s house came after Frank told him about the skips in the punches (Brief of Evidence, 1). On re-cross, however, Black admitted he had become confused over the sequence and said:

“I am so crossed up and worried that I don’t know where I am at.”

He then added:

“I think to the best of my knowledge it was Monday that Frank said that the slips had been changed” (Brief of Evidence, 1).

The Atlanta Journal, Thursday, July 31, 1913, page 6, column 1, reported Black putting the connection even more plainly during the courtroom exchange:

“I remember on one occasion Frank said the slips were mispunched, and that was what caused me to go to Lee’s house” (AJ, 3).

Black was shaky on the exact timing of every conversation. There is no reason to hide it.

But he repeatedly connected Frank’s discussion of the missing punches with police turning their attention toward Lee’s home.

Darley Later Could Not Identify Which Slip Was the Original

There is another loose end.

During N. V. Darley’s Friday, August 1, 1913 trial testimony, Solicitor Dorsey showed him two time-clock slips.

The Atlanta Journal, Saturday, August 2, 1913, reported that one carried the typed date “April 28.” Dorsey asked Darley if it could have been the slip taken out Sunday morning.

Darley said the Sunday slip should have been dated April 26.

The second slip had a handwritten date. Darley could not positively identify either one as the original Sunday-morning slip.

The Journal said the State’s questioning indicated it might contend that the slip eventually given to police was not the original slip removed Sunday morning (AJ, 3). That last part was the newspaper’s description of the prosecution’s line of questioning, not Darley testifying that he knew a substitution had occurred.

Still, it adds another problem.

The man who stood over Frank’s shoulder Sunday morning and examined the original card could not later identify either of the slips put in front of him as the one he had seen.

Frank’s Explanation

Frank did have an answer.

In his unsworn statement to the jury on Monday, August 18, 1913, he said he and Darley had only looked casually down the numbered side of the slip. They saw no numbered line skipped, so they assumed Lee had made all his punches.

Frank said that when he later studied the actual times carefully, he discovered an hour-long interval on three occasions (Brief of Evidence, 1).

That explanation is possible.

It also explains why Darley could say Sunday that the card looked right while later acknowledging three long gaps.

But it does not explain away Rogers so easily.

Rogers independently looked at the slip. He remembered the first punch as 6:01 and the second as 6:32 or 6:33, and said he glanced all the way down and saw “a punch for every number.”

Nor does Frank’s explanation change the Sunday-to-Monday reversal documented by Lee and Black.

What the State Said Happened

By the trial, Solicitor General Hugh Dorsey was not being subtle about the State’s theory.

During the Wednesday afternoon, July 30, 1913 session, Dorsey told Judge Leonard S. Roan:

“I want to show that Frank was trying to point suspicion at Newt Lee.”

Speaking about the bloody shirt, he said:

“Our contention is that this shirt was a plant” and “The shirt was a part of the scheme” (AJ, 3).

Special prosecutor Frank A. Hooper went even harder in closing argument on Thursday, August 21, 1913.

The Atlanta Constitution, Friday, August 22, 1913, page 2, reported Hooper holding the time slip up before the jury and arguing that Frank first said it cleared Lee, then later claimed gaps appeared that gave Lee enough time to go home.

Hooper then turned to the bloody shirt and said:

“It had to be planted. Gentlemen, it was planted!”

He told the jury:

“If Newt Lee was to be made the goat, suspicion had to be directed to him. Somebody had to plant that suspicion” (AC, 4).

That was prosecution argument, not eyewitness testimony. But it tells us exactly how the State understood the time-card evidence.

Who Actually Saw the Before-and-After Change?

Strip everything else away and the witness chain is pretty tight.

Newt Lee was standing at the clock Sunday. Frank told him he had missed no punches. At the April 30 coroner’s inquest, Lee testified that Frank told him Sunday the clock had been punched all right, but on Monday morning told him the clock had not been punched right.

W. W. “Boots” Rogers personally examined the Sunday slip. He saw the first punches at approximately 6:01 and 6:32 or 6:33 and testified that there was “a punch for every number.” He saw Frank take the slip back into his office.

N. V. Darley stood over Frank’s shoulder Sunday and “verified” Frank’s statement that the card was all right. He later acknowledged the long intervals he had failed to notice and later could not positively identify which of two slips shown to him was the original Sunday card.

Detective John R. Black saw Frank remove the card Sunday and heard Frank say it had been punched correctly. Black then testified that on Monday and Tuesday Frank said the clock had been mispunched three times. Frank told Black the missing time gave Lee enough time to go home and return.

Chief Newport A. Lanford was placed at the Sunday clock-opening by Newt Lee. The later custody of the card becomes disputed because Frank said Lanford took it Sunday, while Black could not personally say when Lanford received it.

Those are the witnesses who build the time-card issue.

The strongest argument is not that somebody saw Frank standing over the card with an eraser. Nobody testified to that.

The stronger argument is harder to get around.

On Sunday morning, in front of several people, the card was pronounced correct.

Frank then had physical access to it and it remained in his custody.

By Monday, he was describing the same record as incorrect.

The newly discovered missing time of four hours conveniently gave Newt Lee an opportunity to go home.

On Tuesday morning police searched Lee’s home and found a bloody shirt.

That is why Newt Lee told The Atlanta Georgian on Wednesday, April 30, 1913 that it looked like Frank was trying to put the crime on him.

And it is why the prosecution later argued that the time slip and bloody shirt were not two unrelated oddities. They were parts of the same attempt to turn the investigation toward Newt Lee.

text:
AP Police impersonated the FBI

Subject: Request for Investigation - Andhra Pradesh Police Officer Identified “FBI” as Requesting Organization in X/Twitter Law-Enforcement Request Concerning a U.S. Citizen

To:
Director, Federal Bureau of Investigation
The Internet Crime Complaint Center (IC3)
@FBI @FBIDirectorKash @FBITampa @TheJusticeDept  
U.S. Department of Justice

Dear Director / Appropriate Federal Officials:

I am a United States citizen residing in the United States. I respectfully submit this complaint and request for review concerning an apparent misrepresentation of U.S. federal law-enforcement identity in connection with a social-media investigation initiated by the Andhra Pradesh Police in India.

I. Summary of the complaint

I recently received a notification from X Support concerning a law-enforcement request submitted to X regarding my X account.
The X communication initially stated that the request had been submitted by the “FBI.”

However, X subsequently provided an important correction. X expressly stated:

“However, this request did not come from the U.S. Federal Bureau of Investigation (FBI)”

X further stated that the request actually came from the Andhra Pradesh Police and identified the submitting individual as:

Name: A V Bramham
Position: Inspector of Police
Organization entered by requester: FBI
Email: guntururbansp-ap@gov.in
Location: Guntur, Andhra Pradesh, India
Country: India

X further stated:
“it is unclear why the Andhra Pradesh Police wrote ‘FBI’ as the sender organization.”
I have preserved the X communication and can provide the original notification and screenshot as evidence.
II. Why I am requesting U.S. government review
I fully recognize that foreign law-enforcement agencies may communicate with U.S. companies through legitimate international law-enforcement cooperation channels.
The issue here is different.

According to X’s own records, an Andhra Pradesh Police official submitted the request, but the requesting organization was entered as “FBI.”

I therefore respectfully request that the appropriate U.S. authorities determine:

Whether the FBI had any involvement whatsoever in this request to X.

Whether any FBI office, agent, liaison officer, or other U.S. government agency authorized, participated in, or communicated with Andhra Pradesh Police concerning my X account.
Whether the Andhra Pradesh Police official knowingly or inadvertently represented himself or his agency as the FBI when submitting the request to X.

Whether the use of “FBI” as the requesting organization was intended to obtain greater credibility, priority, cooperation, disclosure, restriction, or removal of content from X.

Whether X received any other law-enforcement request from Andhra Pradesh Police concerning my account in which the FBI was similarly identified.

Whether this conduct implicates any U.S. federal criminal, civil-rights, cyber, impersonation, transnational-repression, or other federal jurisdiction.

Whether the conduct should be referred to another appropriate federal authority for investigation.
III. First Amendment / transnational-repression concern
The underlying matter concerns social-media content posted on X and alleged violations of Indian law.
I am particularly concerned because I am a U.S. citizen residing in the United States, and the governmental action concerns my online speech and political commentary.
I understand that the United States cannot simply disregard legitimate foreign criminal investigations. However, I am requesting that U.S. authorities determine whether a foreign law-enforcement agency has attempted to use the identity or authority of a U.S. federal agency to influence or restrict constitutionally protected activity occurring in the United States.
The FBI itself recognizes transnational repression as an issue that may affect people in the United States and specifically directs individuals who believe they have been affected by transnational repression to report the matter to the FBI.
IV. Request for preservation and investigation of evidence
I respectfully request that the appropriate agency consider preserving and/or obtaining, where legally appropriate:
the original law-enforcement request submitted by Andhra Pradesh Police to X;

all metadata associated with that request;

the identity and authentication information associated with the requester;

the date and time of submission;

all representations made by the requester concerning his identity and governmental organization;
any attachments, legal documents, FIRs, court orders, or other materials submitted to X;

any subsequent communications between X and Andhra Pradesh Police concerning my account;
any communications between U.S. government agencies and Andhra Pradesh Police concerning this matter; and
any evidence showing whether “FBI” was entered intentionally or accidentally.
V. Request for clarification from the FBI
I respectfully request confirmation of the following:
Did the FBI have any involvement in, authorization of, or knowledge of this particular request to X?
If the answer is no, I respectfully request that the FBI consider whether the circumstances warrant investigation or referral concerning the apparent use of the FBI’s identity by a foreign law-enforcement official.
VI. Good-faith submission
I am not asking the U.S. government to interfere with a legitimate Indian criminal investigation.
My request is narrower:
I am asking the United States government to determine whether an Indian police official represented himself or his agency as the FBI when submitting a law-enforcement request concerning a U.S. citizen’s social-media account, and whether that conduct violated any U.S. law or raised a transnational-repression or foreign-government intimidation concern.

I am prepared to provide the original X communication, screenshots, account information, relevant posts, and any notices received from Andhra Pradesh Police.

I respectfully request that this complaint be logged, reviewed, and referred to the appropriate federal authority if the receiving office does not have jurisdiction.

Thank you for your attention to this matter.
Respectfully,

U.S. Citizen
@tollywood

Suo motto statement by EAM @DrSJaishankar today on #Bangladesh

“I rise to apprise this august House of certain recent developments pertaining to Bangladesh. As Hon’ble Members are aware, India-Bangladesh relations have been exceptionally close for many decades over many governments. Concern about recent violence and instability there is shared across the political spectrum. 
 
Since the election in January 2024, there has been considerable tensions, deep divides and growing polarization in Bangladesh politics. This underlying foundation aggravated a student agitation that started in June this year. There was growing violence, including attacks on public buildings and infrastructure, as well as traffic and rail obstructions. The violence continued through the month of July. Throughout this period, we repeatedly counselled restraint and urged that the situation be defused through dialogue. Similar urgings were made to various political forces with whom we were in touch.
 
Sir, despite a Supreme Court judgement on 21 July, there was no let-up in the public agitation. Various decisions and actions taken thereafter only exacerbated the situation. The agitation at this stage coalesced around a one-point agenda, that is that the Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina should step down. 
 
On 4th August, events took a very serious turn. Attacks on police, including police stations and government installations, intensified even as overall levels of violence greatly escalated. Properties of individuals associated with the regime were torched across the country. What was particularly worrying was that minorities, their businesses and temples also came under attack at multiple locations. The full extent of this is still not clear. 
 
Sir, On 5th August, demonstrators converged in Dhaka despite the curfew. Our understanding is that after a meeting with leaders of the security establishment, Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina apparently made the decision to resign. At very short notice, she requested approval to come for the moment to India. We simultaneously received a request for flight clearance from Bangladesh authorities. She arrived yesterday evening in Delhi. 
 
The situation in Bangladesh Sir, is still evolving. The Army Chief, General Waker-uz-Zaman, addressed the nation on 5th August. He spoke about assuming responsibility and constituting an interim government.
 
We are in close and continuous touch with the Indian community in Bangladesh through our diplomatic missions. There are an estimated 19,000 Indian nationals there, of which about 9,000 are students. The bulk of the students have already returned to India in the month of July on the advice of the High Commission. In terms of our diplomatic presence, in addition to the High Commission in Dhaka, we have Assistant High Commissions in Chittagong, Rajshahi, Khulna and Sylhet. It is our expectation that the host government will provide the required security protection for these establishments. We look forward to their normal functioning once the situation stabilizes.
 
Chairman Sir, we are also monitoring the situation with regard to the status of minorities. There are reports of initiatives by various groups and organizations to ensure their protection and well-being. We welcome that, but will naturally remain deeply concerned till law and order is visibly restored. Our border guarding forces have also been instructed to be exceptionally alert in view of this complex situation. 
 
In the last 24 hours, we have also been in regular touch with the authorities in Dhaka. This is the situation as of now. I seek the understanding and support of the House in regard to sensitive issues regarding an important neighbour on which there has always been strong national consensus.”

Dear @raghav_chadha ,

I know you are doing very well in Parliament by raising small issues that were ignored by most Members of Parliament but have a bigger impact.

I am writing this post regarding an account lien and bank freeze by the Cyber Police of India.

In my case, the issue started when I received a message from my bank branch stating that my account had received a police notice of lien of 6000 rupees. I immediately went to my bank branch and asked them why my account had a lien of 6000 rupees. They followed some procedure and gave me a printout which contained the acknowledgement of my lien. One of the bank employees told me that I should contact the cyber police mentioned on the paper and provide them with the details of the 6000 rupees, such as where it came from and for what reason. However, they did not give me any specific reason why my bank account had received the lien.

Later, I checked my bank statement to find the details of the 6000 rupees transaction and noticed that my case was reported on 6 December 2025, and I had received a transaction of 6000 rupees on the same date. I remember that my neighbour had sent me this 6000 rupees and asked me to withdraw it from the ATM because he had an urgent situation as his mother was going to her village due to an emergency. As a friend, I withdrew the money and gave it to him.

Now I have all the proofs and details to explain to the police, so I emailed all the details to the Bangalore Cyber Cell or the police station where my notice was issued, as mentioned in the acknowledgement given by my bank. However, I did not receive any response. I then tried to contact the investigation officer mentioned in the report. I called several times, keeping a gap of five to six hours out of respect for his time and duties, as they may have many other responsibilities. I also sent him a message on WhatsApp, but there was still no response.

After four to five days, I called again, and this time he picked up the call. He was speaking in the local language, which I did not understand, as I am from Maharashtra and not familiar with the local language of Bangalore. I then started speaking in English, and he told me that I have to come to Bangalore and verify my documents. I explained that for 6000 rupees, it would not be beneficial for me to travel to Bangalore because transportation, food, and stay would cost more than 6000 rupees. He said that he does not know and that I have to come, otherwise he will not issue the No Objection Certificate, and then he ended the call.

This issue may look small, but similar issues are happening everywhere, and no one is noticing them. It feels like “Kare koi aur bhare koi.” Many innocent people face this issue, and it remains unresolved. Because of chain transactions that come into accounts, some people are unable to use their own money. If I travel, I will have to spend more than 6000 rupees to remove the lien. I believe this issue can be resolved through email or online verification, but the investigation officer denied it.

I am also tagging Pushpendra Sir @pushpendrakum and Bangalore Cyber Police @BlrCityPolice . If you could please look into this matter.

Thank you.

text:
IFF statement against the Alarming Escalation of Social Media Censorship and Proposed Expansion of Takedown Powers

New Delhi, March 19, 2026

The Internet Freedom Foundation (IFF) is concerned by continuing reports of posts and accounts being withheld in India on Facebook, X and Instagram, including satire and criticism of the government. Recent reporting shows users receiving generic “withheld in India” notices or emails under Section 69A from social media platforms, with little or no explanation, while independent reporting has documented takedowns affecting speech that appears political, satirical, or critical rather than clearly unlawful.

As reported by Business Standard and The Indian Express on March 18, the Union Government is currently exploring a proposal to decentralize content blocking powers under Section 69A of the IT Act. The new proposal would grant direct takedown powers to multiple ministries, including Defence, Home Affairs, External Affairs, and Information & Broadcasting. At present, MeitY signs off on Section 69A orders, while a separate notice and takedown channel already operates through Section 79(3)(b) and the Home Ministry led Sahyog portal that at least has 35 nodal officers across State Police Departments in India.

At the same time, the February 2026 amendments to the IT Rules have sharply compressed compliance timelines. MeitY’s own published FAQ says intermediaries must act within 3 hours when they receive actual knowledge through a court order or a government intimation, within 36 hours for certain expedited grievances, and within 2 hours for specified complaints involving nudity, sexual content, morphed content, and impersonation. The government has also reiterated that intermediaries which fail to observe due diligence risk losing Section 79 immunity. A system built on speed, legal threat, and secrecy predictably incentivises over compliance.

We remind the Union Government that the Supreme Court upheld Section 69A in the Shreya Singhal case on the basis of procedural safeguards and written reasons that could be challenged. Secret and inaccessible censorship defeats those safeguards in practice. 

IFF calls on the Union government to halt any move to decentralise Section 69A blocking powers further, publish blocking orders with only as per the letter and spirit of the Shreya Singhal judgement, and ensure timely notice to affected users with clear grounds and avenues for remedy. Platforms must also do more than send boilerplate messages. They should provide meaningful notice, preserve records for challenge, and publish granular transparency reporting given online censorship also impacts the public right to receive information.

If your account or post has been withheld or blocked in India, please write to legal@internetfreedom.in with screenshots, URLs, and any email or platform notice you have received. IFF will try to assist impacted users and document patterns of opaque censorship.

Bhai aur beheno, agar aap bhi Binance P2P trading karte ho aur suddenly bank account freeze ho gaya hai toh pareshan mat ho. Yeh bahut common problem hai India mein. Innocent log bhi fas jaate hain jab kisi buyer/seller ka paisa kisi fraud case se link hota hai.

Yeh steps follow karo - 

1️⃣ Sabse Pehle Bank Branch Jaao  
   - Freeze ka exact reason, Cyber Crime complaint number, IO naam aur Police Station details lo.  
   - Written notice maang lo.

2️⃣ Saare Proofs Collect Karo (Bahut Important)  
   - Binance P2P complete order history (screenshots)  
   - Buyer/Seller ke saath chat  
   - Payment proof (UPI, bank transfer screenshot)  
   - Bank statement jisme transaction dikhe  
   - Aadhaar, PAN, Binance account details

3️⃣ Binance Support ko turant contact karo  
   - App mein Help section → Submit ticket  
   - Order ID aur proofs attach karo. Woh counterparty ko investigate kar sakte hain.

4️⃣ Cyber Cell mein Representation Daalo  
   - Local Cyber Police Station ya online portal pe jaao.  
   - Detailed application likho ki transaction genuine tha Binance P2P pe hua.  
   - Saare proofs attach karo.  
   - Lawyer (Cyber crime specialist) ki madad le lo - yeh bahut kaam aata hai.

5️⃣ Follow-up karte raho  
   - Har 7-10 din mein bank aur cyber cell ko call/email karo.  
   - Partial release ke liye request kar sakte ho.

Extra Tips jo future mein bacha sakte hain:
• P2P ke liye alag dedicated bank account use karo (savings account mat use karo)
• Sirf verified buyers/sellers ke saath trade karo
• Video verification ya proper KYC maango
• Bahut bade amounts ek baar mein mat trade karo
• Binance P2P risky hai India mein, agar ho sake toh avoid karo

Tag your friends jo P2P karte hain! 

#BinanceP2P #BankAccountFreeze #CyberCrimeIndia #P2PScam #CryptoIndia #BinanceFreeze #BankFreezeSolution

Dear @raghav_chadha ,

I know you are doing very well in Parliament by raising small issues that were ignored by most Members of Parliament but have a bigger impact.

I am writing this post regarding an account lien and bank freeze by the Cyber Police of India.

In my case, the issue started when I received a message from my bank branch stating that my account had received a police notice of lien of 6000 rupees. I immediately went to my bank branch and asked them why my account had a lien of 6000 rupees. They followed some procedure and gave me a printout which contained the acknowledgement of my lien. One of the bank employees told me that I should contact the cyber police mentioned on the paper and provide them with the details of the 6000 rupees, such as where it came from and for what reason. However, they did not give me any specific reason why my bank account had received the lien.

Later, I checked my bank statement to find the details of the 6000 rupees transaction and noticed that my case was reported on 6 December 2025, and I had received a transaction of 6000 rupees on the same date. I remember that my neighbour had sent me this 6000 rupees and asked me to withdraw it from the ATM because he had an urgent situation as his mother was going to her village due to an emergency. As a friend, I withdrew the money and gave it to him.

Now I have all the proofs and details to explain to the police, so I emailed all the details to the Bangalore Cyber Cell or the police station where my notice was issued, as mentioned in the acknowledgement given by my bank. However, I did not receive any response. I then tried to contact the investigation officer mentioned in the report. I called several times, keeping a gap of five to six hours out of respect for his time and duties, as they may have many other responsibilities. I also sent him a message on WhatsApp, but there was still no response.

After four to five days, I called again, and this time he picked up the call. He was speaking in the local language, which I did not understand, as I am from Maharashtra and not familiar with the local language of Bangalore. I then started speaking in English, and he told me that I have to come to Bangalore and verify my documents. I explained that for 6000 rupees, it would not be beneficial for me to travel to Bangalore because transportation, food, and stay would cost more than 6000 rupees. He said that he does not know and that I have to come, otherwise he will not issue the No Objection Certificate, and then he ended the call.

This issue may look small, but similar issues are happening everywhere, and no one is noticing them. It feels like “Kare koi aur bhare koi.” Many innocent people face this issue, and it remains unresolved. Because of chain transactions that come into accounts, some people are unable to use their own money. If I travel, I will have to spend more than 6000 rupees to remove the lien. I believe this issue can be resolved through email or online verification, but the investigation officer denied it.

I am also tagging Pushpendra Sir @pushpendrakum and Bangalore Cyber Police @BlrCityPolice . If you could please look into this matter.

Thank you.

is the ECI compromised?  
 In March 2026, ahead of the Kerala Assembly elections (polling on 9 April 2026), a 2019 Election Commission of India (ECI) letter redistributed by the Kerala Chief Electoral Officer’s (CEO) office was found to carry the seal of the BJP’s Kerala unit. This sparked a political row, followed by police-directed efforts to remove related social media posts

This takedown action itself became controversial, with critics framing it as an attempt to suppress discussion of an official lapse during an election period, while authorities maintained it was necessary to stop the circulation of a withdrawn and erroneous document that was being used to question the ECI’s credibility.The episode remained a flashpoint in the final stretch of the Kerala campaign, with the ECI treating it as a corrected administrative mistake and the opposition presenting it as evidence of deeper concerns about the poll body’s independence.The letter and the seal
The document was an ECI communication dated 19 March 2019 containing guidelines/FAQs on the publicity of candidates’ criminal antecedents (following a Supreme Court judgment). CPI(M) and Congress shared versions online showing the BJP Kerala unit’s seal. It had been circulated by the Kerala CEO’s office to political parties, District Election Officers, and Returning Officers as part of clarifications around mid-March 2026.thesouthfirst.comKerala CEO / ECI explanation:
It was described as a “purely clerical error.” The BJP Kerala unit had approached the CEO’s office seeking clarification on the (by then revised) 2019 guidelines and submitted a photocopy of the original directive that already bore the party’s seal. Staff overlooked this and redistributed that version. The error was identified; on 21 March a formal withdrawal notice was issued telling recipients to disregard the document. An Assistant Section Officer was suspended pending inquiry. Later, a Deputy CEO and a Section Officer were relieved of election-related duties.livemint.comOpposition parties (CPI(M) and Congress) rejected the clerical-error account. They alleged compromised institutional neutrality, claiming seals were being “casually swapped” and questioning whether the ECI and BJP shared the same “power centre.” Some BJP responses labelled the circulation of the old document as misinformation or a political plot.thewire.inDeletion of posts controversyActing on an ECI directive (under the Model Code of Conduct), the Kerala Police cyber cell issued notices to X (Twitter), Facebook, Instagram, and numerous individual accounts. They demanded removal of posts sharing the letter that carried the BJP seal.  Police argued the content insulted the Election Commission, undermined its integrity and transparency, spread false claims about a rectified clerical error, and risked public order or communal harmony by potentially fuelling political division. Reports indicated hundreds of accounts were flagged (approximately 270 on X, 200 on Facebook, and 90 on Instagram). A stand-up comedian had two of his original Instagram reels removed after anonymous accounts filed copyright complaints using the same generic Turkish-language text, without identifying any allegedly infringed work. It took a Delhi High Court case for Meta to restore both reels. (1/10)

Read More: https://t.co/RukNwsovEw

But restoration is not the end of the issue. The High Court order does not record that the copyright strikes themselves have been expunged. The questions of removing those strikes and preventing Meta from taking adverse action against Pulkit's page on their basis remain before the Court. (9/10)

This case shows what happens when copyright enforcement becomes the easiest route to getting content removed. A platform says complaints are reviewed and only valid reports are acted upon. Yet two vague complaints were enough to remove content, while repeated appeals produced no reasoned response for months. If the correct decision could be reached once a case entered court, why was it unavailable through the platform's own grievance system?

IFF will continue pushing for meaningful verification of copyright claims, reasoned decisions on appeals within the IT Rules' timelines, and greater transparency around takedowns and reversals. (10/10)

Can we talk about Meta's glasses for a second?

They look like ordinary sunglasses, and the only warning is a tiny LED most people never notice. In just three weeks, we've sent two legal notices to Meta. One is for a man secretly filmed and mocked at a Delhi café. The other is for a woman covertly recorded on her walk home for a "pickup artist's" Instagram content.

Being in public shouldn't mean becoming someone's content without your consent. This is NOT normal.

Phone jammers 👇🏽👇🏽

quotedTweet.text:
There is a crucial difference between an internet shutdown and a phone jammer. An internet shutdown requires a written order under the Telecommunications Act. A jammer is a radio transmitter that can cut voice calls, SMS and mobile data for everyone within its range. So who gives the Delhi Police the power to switch one on? (1/10)
Read More: https://t.co/kU0KOf2fOY

text:
There is a crucial difference between an internet shutdown and a phone jammer. An internet shutdown requires a written order under the Telecommunications Act. A jammer is a radio transmitter that can cut voice calls, SMS and mobile data for everyone within its range. So who gives the Delhi Police the power to switch one on? (1/10)
Read More: https://t.co/kU0KOf2fOY

On 8 September, IFF filed three RTIs with the Delhi Police. We are seeking records on every jammer it possesses, the permissions and procurement documents, the officers authorised to deploy them, the applicable SOPs and deployment registers, and the specific records concerning Jantar Mantar on 20 and 22 July. We have also asked for the records behind the Satya Niketan denial. (9/10)

The question is not whether telecommunications can ever be restricted. Indian law already provides a framework for temporary suspension of services. The question is whether a separate, less visible mechanism can bypass those safeguards and cut communications without the written order, publication, review and accountability that accompany a lawful shutdown. IFF will publish the Delhi Police's replies, including any silence, and continue seeking clarity on who can jam communications, for what purpose and under what law. (10/10)

Support our work: https://t.co/qSG7IzUpIX

This matters because the Delhi Police has powers to regulate public assemblies under the Delhi Police Act, and urgent powers exist under Section 163 of the BNSS. But neither provision gives the police a power to jam telecommunications. In *Anuradha Bhasin*, the Supreme Court held that telecommunications can be suspended only through the legally prescribed framework. Section 163 cannot become a substitute for that framework. (6/10)

There is also a basic rights problem. RML Hospital received injured police personnel after clashes near Jantar Mantar on 22 July, and RML and Lady Hardinge are within roughly two kilometres of the protest site. A jammer that cuts ordinary phone service can also cut a person's ability to call 112, a hospital or family. It can also prevent journalists and citizens from transmitting what is happening at a public assembly. (7/10)

Ray-Ban Meta glasses struck again. A woman walking home alone was secretly recorded by a man who approached her, then posted the footage on Instagram alongside similar clips of him doing this to other women, as part of "pickup" content.

She's filed a police complaint for stalking and voyeurism. IFF is assisting her with a legal notice to the creator, Instagram, and Meta, the second such notice against Meta in India.

This isn't a one off. It's a design problem.
Read more about it: https://t.co/x5Gzp2NFF0

A woman was followed, stopped on a dark street, secretly recorded through Ray-Ban Meta glasses and turned into an Instagram “pickup” reel that reached over 23 lakh views. Now, our legal notice seeks accountability from both him and Meta. (1/10)

Read More: https://t.co/x5Gzp2NFF0

The legal notice therefore puts Meta on notice not merely as the platform hosting the video, but as the designer, developer, manufacturer, marketer and seller of the glasses. It alleges negligence and product liability, arguing that Meta knew about the pattern of misuse but continued selling the device without an effective way for non-users or people being recorded to report that misuse. (9/10)

The notice seeks removal of every copy, preservation and disclosure of evidence, suspension of monetisation, an account of profits, an apology, and ₹2.05 crore in compensatory and exemplary damages. This case raises a larger question: when a company makes a camera that can be worn like ordinary glasses, who protects the person being recorded? Privacy cannot depend on whether the person being filmed has an Instagram account. (10/10)
